Plot an UpSet Chart following WJP style guidelines

Source: R/upsetChart.R
wjp_upset.Rd

wjp_upset() draws an UpSet chart, the alternative to Venn diagrams for many overlapping sets: one bar per intersection of sets (e.g., the unmet needs that people report together), a matrix of dots below the bars that shows which sets form each intersection, and the size of every set as a horizontal bar on the left. Unlike ComplexUpset, which returns a patchwork of several plots, wjp_upset() returns a single ggplot, so the WJP theme, fonts, and wjp_drawn() apply to the whole chart.

Usage

wjp_upset(
  data,
  intersections,
  sets = NULL,
  target,
  labels = NULL,
  set_target = NULL,
  set_labels = NULL,
  order = NULL,
  bar_color = "#482d8b",
  dot_colors = c("#1A1A1A", "#E5E8E8"),
  label_angle = 90,
  sep = " + ",
  width = 468,
  height = 388.8,
  spacing = 10.7,
  set_width_ratio = 0.22,
  bar_ratio = 2/3,
  bar_headroom = 1.25,
  y_title = NULL,
  title_size = 10.75,
  title_colour = "#000000",
  label_size = 10,
  label_colour = "#4D4D4D",
  label_gap = 4.33,
  value_size = 10,
  value_colour = NULL,
  value_fontface = "plain",
  set_value_size = 10,
  set_value_colour = "#1A1A1A",
  dot_radius = 4,
  segment_color = "#000000",
  segment_width = 1.04,
  grid_color = "#EBEBEB",
  grid_width = 1.04,
  ptheme = WJP_theme()
)

Arguments

data

Data frame with one row per intersection.

intersections

String. Column name with the sets of each intersection (string separated by sep, or a list column).

sets

Set names from top to bottom: NULL (default; order of first appearance in intersections), a character vector, or a data frame whose first column holds the set names.

target

String. Column name with the value of each intersection.

labels

String. Column name with the printed value of each intersection. Default is NULL (no values).

set_target

String. Column of sets (a data frame) with the size of each set. Default is NULL (sum of the intersections).

set_labels

String. Column of sets (a data frame) with the printed size of each set. Default is NULL (no size labels).

order

String. Column name with the display order of the intersections (left to right). Default is NULL (data order).

bar_color

String. Color of the intersection and set bars. Default is the WJP primary color "#482d8b".

dot_colors

Character vector of length 2 with the colors of the active and inactive dots of the matrix. Default is c("#1A1A1A", "#E5E8E8").

label_angle

Numeric. Angle of the intersection values. Default is 90 (vertical, reading upwards); 0 prints them horizontally above the bars.

sep

String. Separator of the set names in intersections. Default is " + ".

width, height

Numeric. Size of the chart, in points. Defaults are 468 and 388.8 (6.5 by 5.4 inches).

spacing

Numeric. Outer margin and gap between the bars, the matrix, and the set sizes, in points. Default is 10.7.

set_width_ratio

Numeric. Share of the available width used by the set-size bars. Default is 0.22.

bar_ratio

Numeric. Share of the plotting height used by the intersection bars (the matrix takes the rest). Default is 2/3.

bar_headroom

Numeric. The tallest bar measures 1 / bar_headroom of its panel. Default is 1.25.

y_title

String. Title of the intersection bars (use "\n" for line breaks). Default is NULL (no title).

title_size

Numeric. Size of the title, in points. Default is 10.75.

title_colour

String. Color of the title. Default is "#000000".

label_size

Numeric. Size of the set names, in points. Default is 10.

label_colour

String. Color of the set names. Default is "#4D4D4D".

label_gap

Numeric. Gap between the set names and the matrix, in points. Default is 4.33.

value_size

Numeric. Size of the intersection values, in points. Default is 10.

value_colour

String. Color of the intersection values. Default is NULL (bar_color).

value_fontface

String. Font face of the values. Default is "plain".

set_value_size

Numeric. Size of the set-size labels, in points. Default is 10.

set_value_colour

String. Color of the set-size labels. Default is "#1A1A1A".

dot_radius

Numeric. Radius of the matrix dots, in points. Default is 4.

segment_color

String. Color of the segment joining the active dots. Default is "#000000".

segment_width

Numeric. Width of that segment, in points. Default is 1.04.

grid_color

String. Color of the matrix grid lines (NA for none). Default is "#EBEBEB".

grid_width

Numeric. Width of the grid lines, in points. Default is 1.04.

ptheme

ggplot theme to apply. Default is WJP_theme().

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

The function expects one row per intersection: its sets in intersections (a string with the set names separated by sep, such as "Access to Assistance + Access to Information", or a list column of character vectors), its value in target, and optionally its printed value in labels. Intersections are drawn from left to right in the order of the data, or of the order column.

Sets are listed from top to bottom in the order of sets: a character vector of set names, or a data frame whose first column holds the set names and whose set_target and set_labels columns hold their sizes and printed sizes. When the sizes are not given, a set's size is the sum of the values of the intersections that contain it, and no size label is printed.

The chart is drawn on a canvas of width by height points (the panel of intersection bars on the upper bar_ratio of the plotting height, the matrix below it, and the set sizes on the left), so wjp_save() writes it at that exact size. Each intersection bar is 0.9 of its column, as tall as its value relative to the largest value times bar_headroom.

Examples

# Always load the WJP fonts
wjp_fonts()

# Combinations of unmet needs among people in the justice gap (fictional data)
needs <- data.frame(
  combination = c("Assistance + Information", "Assistance", "Information",
                  "Assistance + Information + Resolution", "Resolution"),
  value       = c(18.2, 14.5, 9.1, 7.4, 2.2)
)
needs$text <- paste0(format(needs$value, nsmall = 1), "%")

set_sizes <- data.frame(
  set  = c("Resolution", "Information", "Assistance"),
  size = c(9.6, 34.7, 40.1)
)
set_sizes$text <- paste0(format(set_sizes$size, nsmall = 1), "%")

wjp_upset(
  needs,
  intersections = "combination",
  sets          = set_sizes,
  target        = "value",
  labels        = "text",
  set_target    = "size",
  set_labels    = "text",
  bar_color     = "#575796",
  y_title       = "% of people within\nthe justice gap"
)
